scoring.title: How points are earned
scoring.intro: The leaderboard compares the average points per game: how many games someone has played doesn't matter — only what came out of them. And a win counts for more the fewer people share it.
scoring.lossHint: Also when nobody wins (draw, abandoned) — the game still counts.
scoring.averageRule: Average = points of all games ÷ number of games. Someone who plays twice as often and does equally well ends up exactly the same — that's why there are no points for showing up or for streaks.
scoring.categoryRule: The win category comes from the game's win label, not from the role card — if you win with the village as the Wolf-Hound, you get village points.
scoring.qualificationRule: You qualify from {minGames, plural, one {# game} other {# games}}, so that no single lucky hit leads the table. Anyone below that runs along in gray, out of competition.
scoring.tiebreakRule: If the averages are equal, the win rate decides; if that is tied too, the rank is shared.
